chapter: Learning the drums and early influences
title: Booker Washington's stick twirling, horns and pistols
summary: Crawford describes how Booker Washington twirled and threw sticks and used squeeze horns and blank pistols while playing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: (inaudible) beat on the top ride cymbal, dump-tickatee-dump-tickatee-dump- toclatee-dump, with that left hand going underneath there with the stick underneath it. I can do that very well. It's still in me, twirling the sticks I got from Booker Washington. Oh, thatman was something

Looked like wheels on his fingers. Throwing them in there, catching them in here, horns, big (inaudible) automobile horns like they used to use on those Packards and whatnot, shooting blank pistols. He did everything.
-- so you mean now he would be playing, and he would be throwing the sticks in the air.
Yeah, and some still coming out on the snaredrum or on the bass drum. He would throw them in there and grab it, keep playing, but something was always going on on the drums. I couldn't understand it.
Everything -- squeeze horns, pistols, blanks. He's playing. You hear a pistol go off. You jump.
And he did -- he did the most amazing things I ever saw.
So now, did he -- what kind of a setup did he have? Did he use a --
A lot of gadgets around these drums. He could squeeze and shoot and all of that, just a regular outfit.
